newsitem.title: FRANCE: French ex-minister sentenced for perjury.
newsitem.headline: French ex-minister sentenced for perjury.

text.p: A French court on Thursday gave ex-cabinet minister Jacques Mellick a year's suspended prison sentence for lying in court to try to shield ex-tycoon Bernard Tapie in a soccer scandal.

The court in the northern town of Valenciennes barred Mellick from running for public office for five years and fined him 30,000 francs ($5,800). The state prosecutor had requested a 15-month suspended sentence.
The ruling ended a case which captivated France and has already landed Tapie in prison for rigging a game between his ex-European champions Marseille and Valenciennes.

Mellick had testified he was in Tapie's Paris office on June 17, 1993, and saw no trace of a soccer coach who testified earlier he was there at the time being bribed by Tapie to take responsibility for the match-rigging.

Mellick's lie was exposed by a picture taken at a ceremony he attended on that day in Valenciennes, where he served as mayor, and by records of motorway toll payments showing he could not have arrived in time for the purported meeting with Tapie.

Mellick confessed during the match-rigging trial that he was lying. He told the Valenciennes court that be had been under pressure from Tapie and agreed to help him so that the tycoon would not close down a factory he had in Valenciennes.

Mellick was also convicted last year of trying to get his office assistant to lie in court to confirm his meeting with Tapie. He was given a two-month suspended sentence on a charge of tampering with a witness and banned for two years from running for public office.

He has resigned his seat in parliament and did not run recently for re-election as Valenciennes mayor. Tapie, also a former cabinet minister, is serving an eight-month jail term over the rigged match.
